Daily Brief

European leaders convened virtually on Ukraine's Independence Day to reaffirm military support for Kyiv, with France pledging interceptor missiles critical to air defense as Russian strikes continue to claim civilian lives at their highest rate since the war's early months [RFI, France 24, BBC]. The meeting of the 'Coalition of the Willing,' co-chaired by Macron, Merz, and new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, comes amid growing concerns over dwindling missile stockpiles across allied nations [The Economist]. Meanwhile, escalating US-Iran tensions dominated economic headlines, with Treasury Secretary Bessent announcing what he termed 'economic D-Day'—a sweeping sanctions offensive—while Iran threatened to shut down Gulf oil exports, further constraining already-reduced Strait of Hormuz traffic [Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. The collapse of US-Canada trade talks triggered fresh 50% tariffs and retaliatory measures, with Prime Minister Carney declaring the two nations 'at war' economically [BBC, Globe and Mail]. In corporate news, Shein launched its long-awaited Hong Kong IPO at a $27 billion valuation, a steep decline from its 2022 peak [BBC, Financial Times, Nikkei Asia].

  • The fast-fashion giant priced its IPO to raise up to $1.77 billion, with shares to begin trading September 1

DRC and M23 Rebels Agree on Peace Roadmap in Swiss-Mediated Talks

  • The Democratic Republic of Congo government and M23 rebels agreed on a roadmap setting out sequenced steps and timelines for peace negotiations
  • Talks held in Switzerland August 17-21 were mediated by the United States, Qatar, Togo, Switzerland, and the African Union Commission
